FACT_ID: sec04-F01 | anchor: A01
Right-of-way is always given and never taken, so drivers yield even when others ignore the rules, with failure-to-yield crashes fining five hundred to two thousand dollars for bodily injury and one thousand to four thousand dollars for serious bodily injury [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F02 | anchor: A01
Signed and signaled intersections demand obedience, one- and two-lane roads yield to divided or three-plus-lane roads, and unpaved roads yield to paved ones [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F03 | anchor: A01
At uncontrolled crossings drivers yield to the right and proceed only when the right runs clear or distant while still checking left, left turns yield to straight-through oncoming traffic, private entries stop ahead of the sidewalk for all vehicles and walkers, and T-intersection endings stop for the through street [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0026]

FACT_ID: sec04-F04 | anchor: A02
Frontage-road drivers yield to vehicles entering or leaving the highway, same-direction multi-lane entries from the right yield to entries from the left, and rail crossings demand a stop fifteen to fifty feet from the nearest rail on signals, gates, flags, devices, trains within about one thousand five hundred feet, audible warnings, or close visible trains [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0027]

FACT_ID: sec04-F05 | anchor: A03
Drivers stay stopped at rail crossings until safe under a fifty-to-two-hundred-dollar fine, treat crossbucks with look-and-listen caution, hold through flashing red until trains pass and lights die, hold lowered gates until trains pass and gates rise, clear every track before crossing, never halt on rails, shove or flee stalled cars by running trackside toward the train, grant trains unstoppable priority, and drop windows and radios to hear whistles [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F06 | anchor: A03
Broken crossing signals go to DPS communications or local officers with the crossing's ID number, and emergencies use the blue-and-white notification sign's railroad number plus the national crossing inventory number and the problem's nature [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F07 | anchor: A03
Siren, bell, or red-light emergency vehicles get the road via a right-edge stop or a slowed clear path, followers stay five hundred feet behind lit fire and ambulance runs, and nobody drives, parks, or blocks around answered alarms [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0028]

FACT_ID: sec04-F08 | anchor: A04
Past a lit stopped emergency vehicle drivers vacate the nearest lane on multi-lane highways, drop twenty below limits of twenty-five or more, or crawl under five below twenty-five, unless an officer directs otherwise [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F09 | anchor: A04
School buses with alternating red lights stop traffic both ways until motion resumes, the driver waves through, or lights quit, except across different roads or controlled-access loading zones without pedestrian crossing, punishing first failures five hundred to one thousand two hundred fifty dollars, repeats within five years one thousand to two thousand dollars with possible six-month suspension, injury crashes as Class A misdemeanors to four thousand dollars and a year in jail, and repeat injury crashes as state jail felonies of one hundred eighty days to two years plus up to ten thousand dollars [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F10 | anchor: A04
Watch for pedestrians whether or not they have priority. Yield at uncontrolled intersections, on WALK, on green without a pedestrian signal, and when the light changes after someone enters the crosswalk. Yield Here signs precede yield lines at marked crosswalks on uncontrolled multilane roads. In-street crossing signs stand at the crosswalk on a center line, lane line or median, never either roadside; overhead crossing signs hang above the road at the crosswalk [A04] [A05].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0029]

FACT_ID: sec04-F11 | anchor: A05
Overhead crossing signs hang above the roadway, pedestrian hybrid beacons fire only at marked crosswalks on push-button demand, and drivers stop on alternating flashing red before going when clear while walkers heed the flashing continue and steady start indications [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec04-F12 | anchor: A05
In-roadway lights embedded in the pavement warn of unseen hazards as a signal alternative guarding midblock, school, uncontrolled, and roundabout-approach crossings [A05].
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0030]
